chunks: This has come upon you because when God alone was invoked you disbelieved; but when partners were associated with Him, you believed. But judgement belongs to God, the all-high and supreme.
ai.seo_question: Why did the hypocrites disbelieve when God was alone but believe when partners were associated with Him?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse highlights the inconsistency of the polytheists of Mecca, who rejected pure monotheism (Tawhid) yet accepted idolatry when it suited their tribal interests, illustrating a fundamental flaw in their spiritual discernment. The conclusion 'Al-Hukm lillah' (Judgment belongs to Allah) serves as a reassurance that divine justice will ultimately rectify this confusion, a theme often linked to the concept of divine authority (Wilayah) in Shia thought. This specific dynamic is frequently cited to contrast the steadfastness of the Ahl al-Bayt with the fickleness of the masses.
